content.english: Ant. The Mother brought forth the King, Whose name is called The Eternal; the joy of a Mother was hers, remaining a Virgin unsullied; neither before nor henceforth hath there been or shall be such another, alleluia.

segments.t: Ant.
Génuit puérpera Regem, cui nomen ætérnum, et gáudia matris habens cum virginitátis honóre: nec primam símilem visa est, nec habére sequéntem, allelúia.

content.latin: Ant. Angelus ad pastóres * ait: Annúntio vobis gáudium magnum: quia natus est vobis hódie Salvátor mundi, allelúia.
content.english: Ant. The Angel said unto the shepherds * I bring you good tidings of great joy; for unto you is born this day a Saviour of the world, alleluia.

segments.t: Ant.
Angelus ad pastóres * ait: Annúntio vobis gáudium magnum: quia natus est vobis hódie Salvátor mundi, allelúia.

content.latin: Psalmus 62 [3]
content.english: Psalm 62 [3]

segments.t: Psalmus 62

content.latin: 62:2 Deus, Deus meus, * ad te de luce vígilo.
content.english: 62:2 O God, my God, * to thee do I watch at break of day.

segments.t: Deus, Deus meus, * ad te de luce vígilo.

content.latin: 62:2 Sitívit in te ánima mea, * quam multiplíciter tibi caro mea.
content.english: 62:2 For thee my soul hath thirsted; * for thee my flesh, O how many ways!

segments.t: Sitívit in te ánima mea, * quam multiplíciter tibi caro mea.

content.latin: 62:3 In terra desérta, et ínvia, et inaquósa: * sic in sancto appárui tibi, ut vidérem virtútem tuam, et glóriam tuam.
content.english: 62:3 In a desert land, and where there is no way, and no water: * so in the sanctuary have I come before thee, to see thy power and thy glory.

segments.t: In terra desérta, et ínvia, et inaquósa: * sic in sancto appárui tibi, ut vidérem virtútem tuam, et glóriam tuam.

content.latin: 62:4 Quóniam mélior est misericórdia tua super vitas: * lábia mea laudábunt te.
content.english: 62:4 For thy mercy is better than lives: * thee my lips shall praise.

segments.t: Quóniam mélior est misericórdia tua super vitas: * lábia mea laudábunt te.

content.latin: 62:5 Sic benedícam te in vita mea: * et in nómine tuo levábo manus meas.
content.english: 62:5 Thus will I bless thee all my life long: * and in thy name I will lift up my hands.

segments.t: Sic benedícam te in vita mea: * et in nómine tuo levábo manus meas.

content.latin: 62:6 Sicut ádipe et pinguédine repleátur ánima mea: * et lábiis exsultatiónis laudábit os meum.
content.english: 62:6 Let my soul be filled as with marrow and fatness: * and my mouth shall praise thee with joyful lips.

segments.t: Sicut ádipe et pinguédine repleátur ánima mea: * et lábiis exsultatiónis laudábit os meum.

content.latin: 62:7 Si memor fui tui super stratum meum, in matutínis meditábor in te: * quia fuísti adiútor meus.
content.english: 62:7 If I have remembered thee upon my bed, I will meditate on thee in the morning: * because thou hast been my helper.

segments.t: Si memor fui tui super stratum meum, in matutínis meditábor in te: * quia fuísti adiútor meus.

content.latin: 62:8 Et in velaménto alárum tuárum exsultábo, adhǽsit ánima mea post te: * me suscépit déxtera tua.
content.english: 62:8 And I will rejoice under the covert of thy wings: my soul hath stuck close to thee: * thy right hand hath received me.

segments.t: Et in velaménto alárum tuárum exsultábo, adhǽsit ánima mea post te: * me suscépit déxtera tua.

content.latin: 62:10 Ipsi vero in vanum quæsiérunt ánimam meam, introíbunt in inferióra terræ: * tradéntur in manus gládii, partes vúlpium erunt.
content.english: 62:10 But they have sought my soul in vain, they shall go into the lower parts of the earth: * they shall be delivered into the hands of the sword, they shall be the portions of foxes.

segments.t: Ipsi vero in vanum quæsiérunt ánimam meam, introíbunt in inferióra terræ: * tradéntur in manus gládii, partes vúlpium erunt.

content.latin: 62:12 Rex vero lætábitur in Deo, laudabúntur omnes qui iurant in eo: * quia obstrúctum est os loquéntium iníqua.
content.english: 62:12 But the king shall rejoice in God, all they shall be praised that swear by him: * because the mouth is stopped of them that speak wicked things.

segments.t: Rex vero lætábitur in Deo, laudabúntur omnes qui iurant in eo: * quia obstrúctum est os loquéntium iníqua.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

segments.t: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

segments.t: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.

Angelus ad pastóres ait: Annúntio vobis gáudium magnum: quia natus est vobis hódie Salvátor mundi, allelúia.

content.latin: Ant. Facta est cum Angelo * multitúdo cæléstis exércitus laudántium Deum, et dicéntium: Glória in excélsis Deo, et in terra pax homínibus bonæ voluntátis, allelúia.
content.english: Ant. There was with the Angel a multitude of the heavenly host, * praising God, and saying Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace, to men of good will, alleluia.

content.latin: Canticum Trium Puerorum [4]
content.english: Canticle of the Three Young Men [4]

segments.t: Canticum Trium Puerorum

content.latin: 3:57 Benedícite, ómnia ópera Dómini, Dómino: * laudáte et superexaltáte eum in sǽcula.
content.english: 3:57 All ye works of the Lord, bless the Lord: * praise and exalt him above all for ever.

segments.t: Benedícite, ómnia ópera Dómini, Dómino: * laudáte et superexaltáte eum in sǽcula.

content.latin: 3:58 Benedícite, Ángeli Dómini, Dómino: * benedícite, cæli, Dómino.
content.english: 3:58 O ye angels of the Lord, bless the Lord: * O ye heavens, bless the Lord:

segments.t: Benedícite, Ángeli Dómini, Dómino: * benedícite, cæli, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:59 Benedícite, aquæ omnes, quæ super cælos sunt, Dómino: * benedícite, omnes virtútes Dómini, Dómino.
content.english: 3:59 O all ye waters that are above the heavens, bless the Lord: * O all ye powers of the Lord, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, aquæ omnes, quæ super cælos sunt, Dómino: * benedícite, omnes virtútes Dómini, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:60 Benedícite, sol et luna, Dómino: * benedícite, stellæ cæli, Dómino.
content.english: 3:60 O ye sun and moon, bless the Lord: * O ye stars of heaven, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, sol et luna, Dómino: * benedícite, stellæ cæli, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:61 Benedícite, omnis imber et ros, Dómino: * benedícite, omnes spíritus Dei, Dómino.
content.english: 3:61 O every shower and dew, bless ye the Lord: * O all ye spirits of God, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, omnis imber et ros, Dómino: * benedícite, omnes spíritus Dei, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:62 Benedícite, ignis et æstus, Dómino: * benedícite, frigus et æstus, Dómino.
content.english: 3:62 O ye fire and heat, bless the Lord: * O ye cold and heat, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, ignis et æstus, Dómino: * benedícite, frigus et æstus, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:63 Benedícite, rores et pruína, Dómino: * benedícite, gelu et frigus, Dómino.
content.english: 3:63 O ye dews and hoar frosts, bless the Lord: * O ye frost and cold, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, rores et pruína, Dómino: * benedícite, gelu et frigus, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:64 Benedícite, glácies et nives, Dómino: * benedícite, noctes et dies, Dómino.
content.english: 3:64 O ye ice and snow, bless the Lord: * O ye nights and days, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, glácies et nives, Dómino: * benedícite, noctes et dies, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:65 Benedícite, lux et ténebræ, Dómino: * benedícite, fúlgura et nubes, Dómino.
content.english: 3:65 O ye light and darkness, bless the Lord: * O ye lightnings and clouds, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, lux et ténebræ, Dómino: * benedícite, fúlgura et nubes, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:66 Benedícat terra Dóminum: * laudet et superexáltet eum in sǽcula.
content.english: 3:66 O let the earth bless the Lord: * let it praise and exalt him above all for ever.

segments.t: Benedícat terra Dóminum: * laudet et superexáltet eum in sǽcula.

content.latin: 3:67 Benedícite, montes et colles, Dómino: * benedícite, univérsa germinántia in terra, Dómino.
content.english: 3:67 O ye mountains and hills, bless the Lord: * O all ye things that spring up in the earth, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, montes et colles, Dómino: * benedícite, univérsa germinántia in terra, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:68 Benedícite, fontes, Dómino: * benedícite, mária et flúmina, Dómino.
content.english: 3:68 O ye fountains, bless the Lord: * O ye seas and rivers, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, fontes, Dómino: * benedícite, mária et flúmina, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:69 Benedícite, cete, et ómnia, quæ movéntur in aquis, Dómino: * benedícite, omnes vólucres cæli, Dómino.
content.english: 3:69 O ye whales, and all that move in the waters, bless the Lord: * O all ye fowls of the air, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, cete, et ómnia, quæ movéntur in aquis, Dómino: * benedícite, omnes vólucres cæli, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:70 Benedícite, omnes béstiæ et pécora, Dómino: * benedícite, fílii hóminum, Dómino.
content.english: 3:70 O all ye beasts and cattle, bless the Lord: * O ye sons of men, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, omnes béstiæ et pécora, Dómino: * benedícite, fílii hóminum, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:71 Benedícat Israël Dóminum: * laudet et superexáltet eum in sǽcula.
content.english: 3:71 O let Israel bless the Lord: * let them praise and exalt him above all for ever.

segments.t: Benedícat Israël Dóminum: * laudet et superexáltet eum in sǽcula.

content.latin: 3:72 Benedícite, sacerdótes Dómini, Dómino: * benedícite, servi Dómini, Dómino.
content.english: 3:72 O ye priests of the Lord, bless the Lord: * O ye servants of the Lord, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, sacerdótes Dómini, Dómino: * benedícite, servi Dómini, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:73 Benedícite, spíritus, et ánimæ iustórum, Dómino: * benedícite, sancti, et húmiles corde, Dómino.
content.english: 3:73 O ye spirits and souls of the just, bless the Lord: * O ye holy and humble of heart, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, spíritus, et ánimæ iustórum, Dómino: * benedícite, sancti, et húmiles corde, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:74 Benedícite, Ananía, Azaría, Mísaël, Dómino: * laudáte et superexaltáte eum in sǽcula.
content.english: 3:74 O Ananias, Azarias, and Misael, bless ye the Lord: * praise and exalt him above all for ever.

segments.t: Benedícite, Ananía, Azaría, Mísaël, Dómino: * laudáte et superexaltáte eum in sǽcula.

content.latin: 3:75 (Fit reverentia:) Benedicámus Patrem et Fílium cum Sancto Spíritu: * laudémus et superexaltémus eum in sǽcula.
content.english: 3:75 (Bow head) Let us bless the Father and the Son, with the Holy Ghost; * let us praise and exalt him above all for ever.

segments.t: 3:75 (Fit reverentia:)
Benedicámus Patrem et Fílium cum Sancto Spíritu: * laudémus et superexaltémus eum in sǽcula.

content.latin: 3:56 Benedíctus es, Dómine, in firmaménto cæli: * et laudábilis, et gloriósus, et superexaltátus in sǽcula.
content.english: 3:56 Blessed art thou, O Lord, in the firmament of heaven: * and worthy of praise, and glorious for ever.

segments.t: Benedíctus es, Dómine, in firmaménto cæli: * et laudábilis, et gloriósus, et superexaltátus in sǽcula.

content.latin: Ant. Facta est cum Angelo multitúdo cæléstis exércitus laudántium Deum, et dicéntium: Glória in excélsis Deo, et in terra pax homínibus bonæ voluntátis, allelúia.
content.english: Ant. There was with the Angel a multitude of the heavenly host, praising God, and saying Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace, to men of good will, alleluia.

segments.t: Ant.
Facta est cum Angelo multitúdo cæléstis exércitus laudántium Deum, et dicéntium: Glória in excélsis Deo, et in terra pax homínibus bonæ voluntátis, allelúia.

content.latin: Ant. Párvulus fílius * hódie natus est nobis: et vocábitur Deus, Fortis, allelúia, allelúia.
content.english: Ant. Unto us this day a little Child is born, * and His name shall be called the Mighty God, alleluia, alleluia.

segments.t: Ant.
Párvulus fílius * hódie natus est nobis: et vocábitur Deus, Fortis, allelúia, allelúia.

content.latin: Psalmus 148 [5]
content.english: Psalm 148 [5]

segments.t: Psalmus 148

content.latin: 148:1 Laudáte Dóminum de cælis: * laudáte eum in excélsis.
content.english: 148:1 Praise ye the Lord from the heavens * praise ye him in the high places.

segments.t: Laudáte Dóminum de cælis: * laudáte eum in excélsis.

content.latin: 148:2 Laudáte eum, omnes Ángeli eius: * laudáte eum, omnes virtútes eius.
content.english: 148:2 Praise ye him, all his angels: * praise ye him, all his hosts.

segments.t: Laudáte eum, omnes Ángeli eius: * laudáte eum, omnes virtútes eius.

content.latin: 148:3 Laudáte eum, sol et luna: * laudáte eum, omnes stellæ et lumen.
content.english: 148:3 Praise ye him, O sun and moon: * praise him, all ye stars and light.

segments.t: Laudáte eum, sol et luna: * laudáte eum, omnes stellæ et lumen.

content.latin: 148:4 Laudáte eum, cæli cælórum: * et aquæ omnes, quæ super cælos sunt, laudent nomen Dómini.
content.english: 148:4 Praise him, ye heavens of heavens: * and let all the waters that are above the heavens, praise the name of the Lord.

segments.t: Laudáte eum, cæli cælórum: * et aquæ omnes, quæ super cælos sunt, laudent nomen Dómini.

content.latin: 148:5 Quia ipse dixit, et facta sunt: * ipse mandávit, et creáta sunt.
content.english: 148:5 For he spoke, and they were made: * he commanded, and they were created.

segments.t: Quia ipse dixit, et facta sunt: * ipse mandávit, et creáta sunt.

content.latin: 148:6 Státuit ea in ætérnum, et in sǽculum sǽculi: * præcéptum pósuit, et non præteríbit.
content.english: 148:6 He hath established them for ever, and for ages of ages: * he hath made a decree, and it shall not pass away.

segments.t: Státuit ea in ætérnum, et in sǽculum sǽculi: * præcéptum pósuit, et non præteríbit.

content.latin: 148:7 Laudáte Dóminum de terra, * dracónes, et omnes abýssi.
content.english: 148:7 Praise the Lord from the earth, * ye dragons, and all ye deeps:

segments.t: Laudáte Dóminum de terra, * dracónes, et omnes abýssi.

content.latin: 148:8 Ignis, grando, nix, glácies, spíritus procellárum: * quæ fáciunt verbum eius:
content.english: 148:8 Fire, hail, snow, ice, stormy winds * which fulfill his word:

segments.t: Ignis, grando, nix, glácies, spíritus procellárum: * quæ fáciunt verbum eius:

content.latin: 148:9 Montes, et omnes colles: * ligna fructífera, et omnes cedri.
content.english: 148:9 Mountains and all hills, * fruitful trees and all cedars:

segments.t: Montes, et omnes colles: * ligna fructífera, et omnes cedri.

content.latin: Kaléndis Ianuárii Luna vicésima tértia Anno Dómini 2027
content.english: The morrow is the Octave of the Birth of our Lord Jesus Christ, upon the which day is commemorated His Circumcision.

content.latin: Octáva Nativitátis Dómini nostri Iesu Christi.
content.english: January 1st 2027, the 23rd day of the Moon, were born into the better life:

content.latin: Circumcísio eiúsdem Dómini nostri Iesu Christi.
content.english: At Rome, the holy martyr Almachius, who was slain by gladiators (about the year 404) at the command of Alpius, prefect of the city, because he said: "This is the Octave of the Lord's Birth, cease from your idolatrous superstitions, and your unclean sacrifices." Likewise at Rome, upon the Appian Way, thirty holy soldiers who were crowned with martyrdom, under the Emperor Diocletian.

content.latin: Romæ pássio sanctæ Martínæ, Vírginis et Mártyris; quæ, sub Alexándro Imperatóre, divérsis tormentórum genéribus cruciáta, tandem, gládio percússa, martýrii palmam adépta est. Ipsíus vero festum tértio Kaléndas Februárii recólitur.
content.english: Likewise at Rome, the holy virgin Martina, who was put to diverse torments, under the Emperor Alexander, and at length gained the crown of martyrdom by the sword, whose feast we keep upon the 30th day of the month of January.

content.latin: Cæsaréæ, in Cappadócia, deposítio sancti Basilíi, cognoménto Magni, Epíscopi, Confessóris et Ecclésiæ Doctóris; qui, témpore Valéntis Imperatóris, doctrína et sapiéntia insignítus omnibúsque virtútibus exornátus, mirabíliter effúlsit, et Ecclésiam advérsus Ariános et Macedoniános inexpugnábili constántia deféndit. Eius autem festívitas potíssimum ágitur décimo octávo Kaléndas Iúlii, quo die Epíscopus ordinátus est.
content.english: At Spoleto, in the time of the Emperor Antonine, the holy martyr, the priest Concordius. He was first cudgelled, then racked, and afterwards suffered imprisonment wherein he was comforted by a visit of angels, and at length was delivered from this life by the sword.

content.latin: Apud montem Senárium, in Etrúria, natális sancti Bonfílii Confessóris, e septem Fundatóribus Ordinis Servórum beátæ Maríæ Vírginis, quam cum idem impénse coluísset, ab ipsa in cælum repénte evocátus est. Illíus porro ac Sociórum festum prídie Idus Februárii celebrátur.
content.english: On the same day, the holy martyr Magnus.

content.latin: Romæ sancti Almáchii Mártyris, qui, cum díceret: «Hodie Octavæ Domínici diéi sunt, cessáte a superstitiónibus idolórum et a sacrifíciis pollútis,» proptérea, iubénte Præfécto Urbis Alípio, a gladiatóribus occísus est.
content.english: At Caesarea, in Cappadocia, the burial of the holy Basil, bishop of Caesarea (in the year 379), whose feast we keep upon the 14th day of June. Which is the day whereon he was ordained a bishop.

content.latin: Item Romæ, via Appia, corónæ sanctórum mílitum trigínta Mártyrum, sub Diocletiáno Imperatóre.
content.english: In Africa, blessed Fulgentius, bishop of the Church of Ruspa (in the year 508), who at the time of the persecution under the Vandals, suffered much at the hands of the Arians because of his Catholic faith, and his eminent teaching. He was exiled to Sardinia (in the year 510); but was at length (in the year 523) allowed to return to his own church, where (in the year 533) he died a holy death, famous for his life and his words.

content.latin: Apud Spolétum sancti Concórdii, Presbýteri et Mártyris; qui, tempóribus Antoníni Imperatóris, primo cæsus fústibus, dehinc equúleo suspénsus, ac póstea macerátus in cárcere, ibíque Angélica visitatióne confortátus, demum gládio vitam finívit.
content.english: At Chieti, in Abruzzo Citeriore, holy Justin, bishop of that city, famous for the holiness of his life, and for the miracles worked through him (in the year 543).

content.latin: Eódem die sancti Magni Mártyris.
content.english: At the monastery of St. Claude, upon the Jura Mountains, in the country of Lyon, holy (4th) Eugendus, Abbot (of Condat), whose life was illustrious for his graces and miracles (in the year 510).

content.latin: In Africa beáti Fulgéntii, Ruspénsis Ecclésiæ Epíscopi, qui, témpore Wandálicæ persecutiónis, ob cathólicam fidem eximiámque doctrínam, ab Ariánis multa perpéssus et in Sardíniam relegátus est; atque tandem, ad própriam Ecclésiam redíre permíssus, vita et verbo clarus, sancto fine quiévit.
content.english: At Senlis (in the year 1049), holy Odilo, (6th) Abbot of Cluny (elected in the year 994), who first commanded that in his monasteries a commemoration of all the faithful departed should be made upon the first day after the festival of All Saints, the which custom the Universal Church hath since approved by adopting it.

content.latin: Teáte, in Aprútio citerióre, natális sancti Iustíni, eiúsdem civitátis Epíscopi, sanctitáte vitæ ac miráculis clari.
content.english: At Monte Senario, in Tuscany, the blessed confessor Bonfiglio, one of the seven founders of the order of servants of the Blessed Virgin Mary, to whom he was devoted and by whom he was suddenly called away to heaven (in the year 1262).

content.latin: In território Lugdunénsi, monastério Iurénsium, sancti Eugéndi Abbátis, cuius vita virtútibus et miráculis plena refúlsit.
content.english: At Alexandria (in the year 470), the burial of the holy virgin Euphrosyne, who shone in her nunnery as a great light by the power of her self-denial and her miracles.

content.latin: Apud Silviníacum, in Gállia, sancti Odilónis, Abbátis Cluniacénsis, qui primus Commemoratiónem ómnium Fidélium Defunctórum, prima die post festum ómnium Sanctórum, in suis monastériis fíeri præcépit; quem ritum póstea universális Ecclésia recípiens comprobávit.
content.english: ℣. And elsewhere many other holy martyrs, confessors, and holy virgins.

content.latin: Romæ natális sancti Vincéntii Maríæ Strambi, Epíscopi Maceraténsis et Tolentíni, Congregatiónis a Cruce et Passióne Iesu sodális, pastoráli zelo præclári, quem Pius Papa Duodécimus inter Sanctos rétulit.

content.latin: 72:1 Quam bonus Israël Deus, his, qui recto sunt corde!
content.english: 72:1 How good is God to Israel, to them that are of a right heart!

segments.t: Quam bonus Israël Deus, his, qui recto sunt corde!

content.latin: 72:2 ‡ Mei autem pæne moti sunt pedes: * pæne effúsi sunt gressus mei.
content.english: 72:2 ‡ But my feet were almost moved; * my steps had wellnigh slipped.

segments.t: Mei autem pæne moti sunt pedes: * pæne effúsi sunt gressus mei.

content.latin: 72:3 Quia zelávi super iníquos, * pacem peccatórum videns.
content.english: 72:3 Because I had a zeal on occasion of the wicked, * seeing the prosperity of sinners.

segments.t: Quia zelávi super iníquos, * pacem peccatórum videns.

content.latin: 72:4 Quia non est respéctus morti eórum: * et firmaméntum in plaga eórum.
content.english: 72:4 For there is no regard to their death, * nor is there strength in their stripes.

segments.t: Quia non est respéctus morti eórum: * et firmaméntum in plaga eórum.

content.latin: 72:5 In labóre hóminum non sunt, * et cum homínibus non flagellabúntur:
content.english: 72:5 They are not in the labour of men: * neither shall they be scourged like other men.

segments.t: In labóre hóminum non sunt, * et cum homínibus non flagellabúntur:

content.latin: 72:6 Ídeo ténuit eos supérbia, * opérti sunt iniquitáte et impietáte sua.
content.english: 72:6 Therefore pride hath held them fast: * they are covered with their iniquity and their wickedness.

segments.t: Ídeo ténuit eos supérbia, * opérti sunt iniquitáte et impietáte sua.

content.latin: 72:7 Pródiit quasi ex ádipe iníquitas eórum: * transiérunt in afféctum cordis.
content.english: 72:7 Their iniquity hath come forth, as it were from fatness: * they have passed into the affection of the heart.

segments.t: Pródiit quasi ex ádipe iníquitas eórum: * transiérunt in afféctum cordis.

content.latin: 72:8 Cogitavérunt, et locúti sunt nequítiam: * iniquitátem in excélso locúti sunt.
content.english: 72:8 They have thought and spoken wickedness: * they have spoken iniquity on high.

segments.t: Cogitavérunt, et locúti sunt nequítiam: * iniquitátem in excélso locúti sunt.

content.latin: 72:9 Posuérunt in cælum os suum: * et lingua eórum transívit in terra.
content.english: 72:9 They have set their mouth against heaven: * and their tongue hath passed through the earth.

segments.t: Posuérunt in cælum os suum: * et lingua eórum transívit in terra.

content.latin: 72:10 Ídeo convertétur pópulus meus hic: * et dies pleni inveniéntur in eis.
content.english: 72:10 Therefore will my people return here * and full days shall be found in them.

segments.t: Ídeo convertétur pópulus meus hic: * et dies pleni inveniéntur in eis.

content.latin: 72:11 Et dixérunt: Quómodo scit Deus, * et si est sciéntia in excélso?
content.english: 72:11 And they said: How doth God know? * and is there knowledge in the most High?

segments.t: Et dixérunt: Quómodo scit Deus, * et si est sciéntia in excélso?

content.latin: 72:12 Ecce, ipsi peccatóres, et abundántes in sǽculo, * obtinuérunt divítias.
content.english: 72:12 Behold these are sinners; and yet abounding in the world * they have obtained riches.

segments.t: Ecce, ipsi peccatóres, et abundántes in sǽculo, * obtinuérunt divítias.

content.latin: 72:13 Et dixi: Ergo sine causa iustificávi cor meum, * et lavi inter innocéntes manus meas:
content.english: 72:13 And I said: Then have I in vain justified my heart, * and washed my hands among the innocent.

segments.t: Et dixi: Ergo sine causa iustificávi cor meum, * et lavi inter innocéntes manus meas:

content.latin: 72:14 Et fui flagellátus tota die, * et castigátio mea in matutínis.
content.english: 72:14 And I have been scourged all the day; * and my chastisement hath been in the mornings.

segments.t: Et fui flagellátus tota die, * et castigátio mea in matutínis.

content.latin: 72:15 Si dicébam: Narrábo sic: * ecce, natiónem filiórum tuórum reprobávi.
content.english: 72:15 If I said: I will speak thus; * behold I should condemn the generation of thy children.

segments.t: Si dicébam: Narrábo sic: * ecce, natiónem filiórum tuórum reprobávi.

content.latin: 72:16 Existimábam ut cognóscerem hoc, * labor est ante me:
content.english: 72:16 I studied that I might know this thing, * it is a labour in my sight:

segments.t: Existimábam ut cognóscerem hoc, * labor est ante me:

content.latin: 72:17 Donec intrem in Sanctuárium Dei: * et intéllegam in novíssimis eórum.
content.english: 72:17 Until I go into the sanctuary of God, * and understand concerning their last ends.

segments.t: Donec intrem in Sanctuárium Dei: * et intéllegam in novíssimis eórum.

Psalmus 72(18-28)

content.latin: 72:18 Verúmtamen propter dolos posuísti eis: * deiecísti eos dum allevaréntur.
content.english: 72:18 But indeed for deceits thou hast put it to them: * when they were lifted up, thou hast cast them down.

segments.t: Verúmtamen propter dolos posuísti eis: * deiecísti eos dum allevaréntur.

content.latin: 72:19 Quómodo facti sunt in desolatiónem, súbito defecérunt: * periérunt propter iniquitátem suam.
content.english: 72:19 How are they brought to desolation? they have suddenly ceased to be: * they have perished by reason of their iniquity.

segments.t: Quómodo facti sunt in desolatiónem, súbito defecérunt: * periérunt propter iniquitátem suam.

content.latin: 72:20 Velut sómnium surgéntium, Dómine, * in civitáte tua imáginem ipsórum ad níhilum rédiges.
content.english: 72:20 As the dream of them that awake, O Lord; * so in thy city thou shalt bring their image to nothing.

segments.t: Velut sómnium surgéntium, Dómine, * in civitáte tua imáginem ipsórum ad níhilum rédiges.

content.latin: 72:21 Quia inflammátum est cor meum, et renes mei commutáti sunt: * et ego ad níhilum redáctus sum, et nescívi.
content.english: 72:21 For my heart hath been inflamed, and my reins have been changed: * and I am brought to nothing, and I knew not.

segments.t: Quia inflammátum est cor meum, et renes mei commutáti sunt: * et ego ad níhilum redáctus sum, et nescívi.

content.latin: 72:23 Ut iuméntum factus sum apud te: * et ego semper tecum.
content.english: 72:23 I am become as a beast before thee: * and I am always with thee.

segments.t: Ut iuméntum factus sum apud te: * et ego semper tecum.

content.latin: 72:24 Tenuísti manum déxteram meam: et in voluntáte tua deduxísti me, * et cum glória suscepísti me.
content.english: 72:24 Thou hast held me by my right hand; and by thy will thou hast conducted me, * and with thy glory thou hast received me.

segments.t: Tenuísti manum déxteram meam: et in voluntáte tua deduxísti me, * et cum glória suscepísti me.

content.latin: 72:25 Quid enim mihi est in cælo? * et a te quid vólui super terram?
content.english: 72:25 For what have I in heaven? * and besides thee what do I desire upon earth?

segments.t: Quid enim mihi est in cælo? * et a te quid vólui super terram?

content.latin: 72:26 Defécit caro mea, et cor meum: * Deus cordis mei, et pars mea Deus in ætérnum.
content.english: 72:26 For thee my flesh and my heart hath fainted away: * thou art the God of my heart, and the God that is my portion for ever.

segments.t: Defécit caro mea, et cor meum: * Deus cordis mei, et pars mea Deus in ætérnum.

content.latin: 72:27 Quia ecce, qui elóngant se a te, períbunt: * perdidísti omnes, qui fornicántur abs te.
content.english: 72:27 For behold they that go far from thee shall perish: * thou hast destroyed all them that are disloyal to thee.

segments.t: Quia ecce, qui elóngant se a te, períbunt: * perdidísti omnes, qui fornicántur abs te.

content.latin: 72:28 Mihi autem adhærére Deo bonum est: * pónere in Dómino Deo spem meam:
content.english: 72:28 But it is good for me to adhere to my God, * to put my hope in the Lord God:

segments.t: Mihi autem adhærére Deo bonum est: * pónere in Dómino Deo spem meam:

content.latin: 72:28 Ut annúntiem omnes prædicatiónes tuas, * in portis fíliæ Sion.
content.english: 72:28 That I may declare all thy praises, * in the gates of the daughter of Sion.

segments.t: Ut annúntiem omnes prædicatiónes tuas, * in portis fíliæ Sion.

content.latin: Multifáriam, multísque modis olim Deus loquens pátribus in prophétis: novíssime diébus istis locútus est nobis in Fílio, quem constítuit herédem universórum, per quem fecit et sǽcula.
content.english: God, who, at sundry times and in diverse manners, spoke in times past to the fathers by the prophets, last of all, in these days hath spoken to us by his Son, whom he hath appointed heir of all things, by whom also he made the world.

content.latin: 73:3 Leva manus tuas in supérbias eórum in finem: * quanta malignátus est inimícus in sancto!
content.english: 73:3 Lift up thy hands against their pride unto the end; * see what things the enemy hath done wickedly in the sanctuary.

segments.t: Leva manus tuas in supérbias eórum in finem: * quanta malignátus est inimícus in sancto!

content.latin: 73:4 Et gloriáti sunt qui odérunt te: * in médio solemnitátis tuæ.
content.english: 73:4 And they that hate thee have made their boasts, * in the midst of thy solemnity.

segments.t: Et gloriáti sunt qui odérunt te: * in médio solemnitátis tuæ.

content.latin: 73:5 Posuérunt signa sua, signa: * et non cognovérunt sicut in éxitu super summum.
content.english: 73:5 They have set up their ensigns for signs, * and they knew not both in the going out and on the highest top.

segments.t: Posuérunt signa sua, signa: * et non cognovérunt sicut in éxitu super summum.

content.latin: 73:6 Quasi in silva lignórum secúribus excidérunt iánuas eius in idípsum: * in secúri et áscia deiecérunt eam.
content.english: 73:6 As with axes in a wood of trees, they have cut down at once the gates thereof, * with axe and hatchet they have brought it down.

segments.t: Quasi in silva lignórum secúribus excidérunt iánuas eius in idípsum: * in secúri et áscia deiecérunt eam.

content.latin: 73:7 Incendérunt igni Sanctuárium tuum: * in terra polluérunt tabernáculum nóminis tui.
content.english: 73:7 They have set fire to thy sanctuary: * they have defiled the dwelling place of thy name on the earth.

segments.t: Incendérunt igni Sanctuárium tuum: * in terra polluérunt tabernáculum nóminis tui.

content.latin: 73:8 Dixérunt in corde suo cognátio eórum simul: * Quiéscere faciámus omnes dies festos Dei a terra.
content.english: 73:8 They said in their heart, the whole kindred of them together: * Let us abolish all the festival days of God from the land.

segments.t: Dixérunt in corde suo cognátio eórum simul: * Quiéscere faciámus omnes dies festos Dei a terra.

content.latin: 73:9 Signa nostra non vídimus, iam non est prophéta: * et nos non cognóscet ámplius.
content.english: 73:9 Our signs we have not seen, there is now no prophet: * and he will know us no more.

segments.t: Signa nostra non vídimus, iam non est prophéta: * et nos non cognóscet ámplius.

content.latin: 73:10 Úsquequo, Deus, improperábit inimícus: * irrítat adversárius nomen tuum in finem?
content.english: 73:10 How long, O God, shall the enemy reproach: * is the adversary to provoke thy name for ever?

segments.t: Úsquequo, Deus, improperábit inimícus: * irrítat adversárius nomen tuum in finem?

content.latin: 73:11 Ut quid avértis manum tuam, et déxteram tuam, * de médio sinu tuo in finem?
content.english: 73:11 Why dost thou turn away thy hand: and thy right hand * out of the midst of thy bosom for ever?

segments.t: Ut quid avértis manum tuam, et déxteram tuam, * de médio sinu tuo in finem?

content.latin: 73:12 Deus autem Rex noster ante sǽcula: * operátus est salútem in médio terræ.
content.english: 73:12 But God is our king before ages: * he hath wrought salvation in the midst of the earth.

segments.t: Deus autem Rex noster ante sǽcula: * operátus est salútem in médio terræ.

content.latin: 73:13 Tu confirmásti in virtúte tua mare: * contribulásti cápita dracónum in aquis.
content.english: 73:13 Thou by thy strength didst make the sea firm: * thou didst crush the heads of the dragons in the waters.

segments.t: Tu confirmásti in virtúte tua mare: * contribulásti cápita dracónum in aquis.

content.latin: 73:14 Tu confregísti cápita dracónis: * dedísti eum escam pópulis Æthíopum.
content.english: 73:14 Thou hast broken the heads of the dragon: * thou hast given him to be meat for the people of the Ethiopians.

segments.t: Tu confregísti cápita dracónis: * dedísti eum escam pópulis Æthíopum.

content.latin: 73:15 Tu dirupísti fontes, et torréntes: * tu siccásti flúvios Ethan.
content.english: 73:15 Thou hast broken up the fountains and the torrents: * thou hast dried up the Ethan rivers.

segments.t: Tu dirupísti fontes, et torréntes: * tu siccásti flúvios Ethan.

content.latin: 73:16 Tuus est dies, et tua est nox: * tu fabricátus es auróram et solem.
content.english: 73:16 Thine is the day, and thine is the night: * thou hast made the morning light and the sun.

segments.t: Tuus est dies, et tua est nox: * tu fabricátus es auróram et solem.

content.latin: 73:17 Tu fecísti omnes términos terræ: * æstátem et ver tu plasmásti ea.
content.english: 73:17 Thou hast made all the borders of the earth: * the summer and the spring were formed by thee.

segments.t: Tu fecísti omnes términos terræ: * æstátem et ver tu plasmásti ea.

content.latin: 73:18 Memor esto huius, inimícus improperávit Dómino: * et pópulus insípiens incitávit nomen tuum.
content.english: 73:18 Remember this, the enemy hath reproached the Lord: * and a foolish people hath provoked thy name.

segments.t: Memor esto huius, inimícus improperávit Dómino: * et pópulus insípiens incitávit nomen tuum.

content.latin: 73:19 Ne tradas béstiis ánimas confiténtes tibi, * et ánimas páuperum tuórum ne obliviscáris in finem.
content.english: 73:19 Deliver not up to beasts the souls that confess to thee: * and forget not to the end the souls of thy poor.

segments.t: Ne tradas béstiis ánimas confiténtes tibi, * et ánimas páuperum tuórum ne obliviscáris in finem.

content.latin: 73:20 Réspice in testaméntum tuum: * quia repléti sunt, qui obscuráti sunt terræ dómibus iniquitátum.
content.english: 73:20 Have regard to thy covenant: * for they that are the obscure of the earth have been filled with dwellings of iniquity.

segments.t: Réspice in testaméntum tuum: * quia repléti sunt, qui obscuráti sunt terræ dómibus iniquitátum.

content.latin: 73:21 Ne avertátur húmilis factus confúsus: * pauper et inops laudábunt nomen tuum.
content.english: 73:21 Let not the humble be turned away with confusion: * the poor and needy shall praise thy name.

segments.t: Ne avertátur húmilis factus confúsus: * pauper et inops laudábunt nomen tuum.

content.latin: 73:22 Exsúrge, Deus, iúdica causam tuam: * memor esto improperiórum tuórum, eórum quæ ab insipiénte sunt tota die.
content.english: 73:22 Arise, O God, judge thy own cause: * remember thy reproaches with which the foolish man hath reproached thee all the day.

segments.t: Exsúrge, Deus, iúdica causam tuam: * memor esto improperiórum tuórum, eórum quæ ab insipiénte sunt tota die.

content.latin: 73:23 Ne obliviscáris voces inimicórum tuórum: * supérbia eórum, qui te odérunt, ascéndit semper.
content.english: 73:23 Forget not the voices of thy enemies: * the pride of them that hate thee ascendeth continually.

segments.t: Ne obliviscáris voces inimicórum tuórum: * supérbia eórum, qui te odérunt, ascéndit semper.

segments.t: Cum exsúrgeret in iudícium Deus, * ut salvos fáceret omnes mansuétos terræ.

content.latin: 75:11 Quóniam cogitátio hóminis confitébitur tibi: * et relíquiæ cogitatiónis diem festum agent tibi.
content.english: 75:11 For the thought of man shall give praise to thee: * and the remainders of the thought shall keep holiday to thee.

segments.t: Quóniam cogitátio hóminis confitébitur tibi: * et relíquiæ cogitatiónis diem festum agent tibi.

content.latin: 75:12 Vovéte, et réddite Dómino, Deo vestro: * omnes, qui in circúitu eius affértis múnera.
content.english: 75:12 Vow ye, and pay to the Lord your God: * all you that are round about him bring presents.

segments.t: Vovéte, et réddite Dómino, Deo vestro: * omnes, qui in circúitu eius affértis múnera.

content.latin: 75:13 Terríbili et ei qui aufert spíritum príncipum, * terríbili apud reges terræ.
content.english: 75:13 To him that is terrible, even to him who taketh away the spirit of princes: * to the terrible with the kings of the earth.

segments.t: Terríbili et ei qui aufert spíritum príncipum, * terríbili apud reges terræ.

content.latin: Ant. Invocábimus nomen tuum, Dómine: narrábimus mirabília tua.
content.english: Ant. We will call upon thy name O Lord. We will relate thy wondrous works.

segments.t: Ant.
Invocábimus nomen tuum, Dómine: narrábimus mirabília tua.

content.latin: Ipsi períbunt, tu autem permanébis; et omnes sicut vestiméntum veteráscent: et velut amíctum mutábis eos, et mutabúntur: tu autem idem ipse es, et anni tui non defícient.
content.english: They shall perish, but thou shalt continue: and they shall all grow old as a garment. And as a vesture shalt thou change them, and they shall be changed: but thou art the selfsame, and thy years shall not fail.

content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

segments.t: Deo grátias.

content.english: ℟.br. All the ends of the earth have seen. * Alleluia, Alleluia.

content.english: ℣. O Lord, hear my prayer.

content.english: ℟. And let my cry come unto thee.

content.latin: Orémus.
content.english: Let us pray.

content.latin: Concéde, quǽsumus, omnípotens Deus: ut nos Unigéniti tui nova per carnem Natívitas líberet; quos sub peccáti iugo vetústa sérvitus tenet.
content.english: Grant, we beseech thee, almighty God, that the new birth of thy Only-begotten Son as man may set us free, who are held by the old bondage under the yoke of sin.

content.latin: Per eúndem Dóminum nostrum Iesum Christum Fílium tuum, qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
content.english: Through the same Jesus Christ, thy Son, Our Lord, Who liveth and reigneth with thee in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end.

content.english: ℟. Amen.

content.english: ℟. O Lord, make haste to help me.

content.english: Ant. O wondrous interchange! * the Creator of mankind, taking upon him a living body, vouchsafed to be born of a pure Virgin: and by his Humanity, which was begotten in no earthly wise, hath made us partakers of his Divinity.

content.english: Psalm 109 [1]

segments.t: Psalmus 109

content.latin: 109:1 Dixit Dóminus Dómino meo: * Sede a dextris meis:
content.english: 109:1 The Lord said to my Lord: * Sit thou at my right hand:

segments.t: Dixit Dóminus Dómino meo: * Sede a dextris meis:

content.latin: 109:1 Donec ponam inimícos tuos, * scabéllum pedum tuórum.
content.english: 109:1 Until I make thy enemies * thy footstool.

segments.t: Donec ponam inimícos tuos, * scabéllum pedum tuórum.

content.latin: 109:2 Virgam virtútis tuæ emíttet Dóminus ex Sion: * domináre in médio inimicórum tuórum.
content.english: 109:2 The Lord will send forth the sceptre of thy power out of Sion: * rule thou in the midst of thy enemies.

segments.t: Virgam virtútis tuæ emíttet Dóminus ex Sion: * domináre in médio inimicórum tuórum.

content.latin: 109:3 Tecum princípium in die virtútis tuæ in splendóribus sanctórum: * ex útero ante lucíferum génui te.
content.english: 109:3 With thee is the principality in the day of thy strength: in the brightness of the saints: * from the womb before the day star I begot thee.

segments.t: Tecum princípium in die virtútis tuæ in splendóribus sanctórum: * ex útero ante lucíferum génui te.

content.latin: 109:4 Iurávit Dóminus, et non pœnitébit eum: * Tu es sacérdos in ætérnum secúndum órdinem Melchísedech.
content.english: 109:4 The Lord hath sworn, and he will not repent: * Thou art a priest for ever according to the order of Melchisedech.

segments.t: Iurávit Dóminus, et non pœnitébit eum: * Tu es sacérdos in ætérnum secúndum órdinem Melchísedech.

content.latin: 109:5 Dóminus a dextris tuis, * confrégit in die iræ suæ reges.
content.english: 109:5 The Lord at thy right hand * hath broken kings in the day of his wrath.

segments.t: Dóminus a dextris tuis, * confrégit in die iræ suæ reges.

content.latin: 109:6 Iudicábit in natiónibus, implébit ruínas: * conquassábit cápita in terra multórum.
content.english: 109:6 He shall judge among nations, he shall fill ruins: * he shall crush the heads in the land of many.

segments.t: Iudicábit in natiónibus, implébit ruínas: * conquassábit cápita in terra multórum.

content.latin: 109:7 De torrénte in via bibet: * proptérea exaltábit caput.
content.english: 109:7 He shall drink of the torrent in the way: * therefore shall he lift up the head.

segments.t: De torrénte in via bibet: * proptérea exaltábit caput.

content.english: Ant. When thou wast born * all ineffably of a Virgin, then were the Scriptures fulfilled; thou camest down like the dew upon the fleece of wool, to bring salvation unto all mankind; we praise thee, O our God.

content.english: Psalm 112 [2]

segments.t: Psalmus 112

content.latin: 112:1 Laudáte, púeri, Dóminum: * laudáte nomen Dómini.
content.english: 112:1 Praise the Lord, ye children: * praise ye the name of the Lord.

segments.t: Laudáte, púeri, Dóminum: * laudáte nomen Dómini.

content.latin: 112:2 (fit reverentia) Sit nomen Dómini benedíctum, * ex hoc nunc, et usque in sǽculum.
content.english: 112:2 (bow head) Blessed be the name of the Lord, * from henceforth now and for ever.

segments.t: 112:2 (fit reverentia)
Sit nomen Dómini benedíctum, * ex hoc nunc, et usque in sǽculum.

content.latin: 112:3 A solis ortu usque ad occásum, * laudábile nomen Dómini.
content.english: 112:3 From the rising of the sun unto the going down of the same, * the name of the Lord is worthy of praise.

segments.t: A solis ortu usque ad occásum, * laudábile nomen Dómini.

content.latin: 112:4 Excélsus super omnes gentes Dóminus, * et super cælos glória eius.
content.english: 112:4 The Lord is high above all nations; * and his glory above the heavens.

segments.t: Excélsus super omnes gentes Dóminus, * et super cælos glória eius.

content.latin: 112:5 Quis sicut Dóminus, Deus noster, qui in altis hábitat, * et humília réspicit in cælo et in terra?
content.english: 112:5 Who is as the Lord our God, who dwelleth on high: * and looketh down on the low things in heaven and in earth?

segments.t: Quis sicut Dóminus, Deus noster, qui in altis hábitat, * et humília réspicit in cælo et in terra?

content.latin: 112:7 Súscitans a terra ínopem, * et de stércore érigens páuperem:
content.english: 112:7 Raising up the needy from the earth, * and lifting up the poor out of the dunghill:

segments.t: Súscitans a terra ínopem, * et de stércore érigens páuperem:

content.latin: 112:8 Ut cóllocet eum cum princípibus, * cum princípibus pópuli sui.
content.english: 112:8 That he may place him with princes, * with the princes of his people.

segments.t: Ut cóllocet eum cum princípibus, * cum princípibus pópuli sui.

content.latin: 112:9 Qui habitáre facit stérilem in domo, * matrem filiórum lætántem.
content.english: 112:9 Who maketh a barren woman to dwell in a house, * the joyful mother of children.

segments.t: Qui habitáre facit stérilem in domo, * matrem filiórum lætántem.

content.latin: Psalmus 121 [3]
content.english: Psalm 121 [3]

segments.t: Psalmus 121

content.latin: 121:1 Lætátus sum in his, quæ dicta sunt mihi: * In domum Dómini íbimus.
content.english: 121:1 I rejoiced at the things that were said to me: * We shall go into the house of the Lord.

segments.t: Lætátus sum in his, quæ dicta sunt mihi: * In domum Dómini íbimus.

content.latin: 121:2 Stantes erant pedes nostri, * in átriis tuis, Ierúsalem.
content.english: 121:2 Our feet were standing * in thy courts, O Jerusalem.

segments.t: Stantes erant pedes nostri, * in átriis tuis, Ierúsalem.

content.latin: 121:3 Ierúsalem, quæ ædificátur ut cívitas: * cuius participátio eius in idípsum.
content.english: 121:3 Jerusalem, which is built as a city, * which is compact together.

segments.t: Ierúsalem, quæ ædificátur ut cívitas: * cuius participátio eius in idípsum.

content.latin: 121:4 Illuc enim ascendérunt tribus, tribus Dómini: * testimónium Israël ad confiténdum nómini Dómini.
content.english: 121:4 For thither did the tribes go up, the tribes of the Lord: * the testimony of Israel, to praise the name of the Lord.

segments.t: Illuc enim ascendérunt tribus, tribus Dómini: * testimónium Israël ad confiténdum nómini Dómini.

content.latin: 121:5 Quia illic sedérunt sedes in iudício, * sedes super domum David.
content.english: 121:5 Because their seats have sat in judgment, * seats upon the house of David.

segments.t: Quia illic sedérunt sedes in iudício, * sedes super domum David.

content.latin: 121:6 Rogáte quæ ad pacem sunt Ierúsalem: * et abundántia diligéntibus te:
content.english: 121:6 Pray ye for the things that are for the peace of Jerusalem: * and abundance for them that love thee.

segments.t: Rogáte quæ ad pacem sunt Ierúsalem: * et abundántia diligéntibus te:

content.latin: 121:7 Fiat pax in virtúte tua: * et abundántia in túrribus tuis.
content.english: 121:7 Let peace be in thy strength: * and abundance in thy towers.

segments.t: Fiat pax in virtúte tua: * et abundántia in túrribus tuis.

content.latin: 121:8 Propter fratres meos, et próximos meos, * loquébar pacem de te:
content.english: 121:8 For the sake of my brethren, and of my neighbours, * I spoke peace of thee.

segments.t: Propter fratres meos, et próximos meos, * loquébar pacem de te:

content.latin: 121:9 Propter domum Dómini, Dei nostri, * quæsívi bona tibi.
content.english: 121:9 Because of the house of the Lord our God, * I have sought good things for thee.

segments.t: Propter domum Dómini, Dei nostri, * quæsívi bona tibi.

content.english: Ant. The Root of Jesse hath budded, * the Star hath come out of Jacob, the Virgin hath borne the Saviour: we praise thee, O our God.

content.latin: Psalmus 126 [4]
content.english: Psalm 126 [4]

segments.t: Psalmus 126

content.latin: 126:1 Nisi Dóminus ædificáverit domum, * in vanum laboravérunt qui ædíficant eam.
content.english: 126:1 Unless the Lord build the house, * they labour in vain that build it.

segments.t: Nisi Dóminus ædificáverit domum, * in vanum laboravérunt qui ædíficant eam.

content.latin: 126:1 Nisi Dóminus custodíerit civitátem, * frustra vígilat qui custódit eam.
content.english: 126:1 Unless the Lord keep the city, * he watcheth in vain that keepeth it.

segments.t: Nisi Dóminus custodíerit civitátem, * frustra vígilat qui custódit eam.

content.latin: 126:2 Vanum est vobis ante lucem súrgere: * súrgite postquam sedéritis, qui manducátis panem dolóris.
content.english: 126:2 It is vain for you to rise before light, * rise ye after you have sitten, you that eat the bread of sorrow.

segments.t: Vanum est vobis ante lucem súrgere: * súrgite postquam sedéritis, qui manducátis panem dolóris.

content.latin: 126:2 Cum déderit diléctis suis somnum: * ecce heréditas Dómini fílii: merces, fructus ventris.
content.english: 126:2 When he shall give sleep to his beloved, * behold the inheritance of the Lord are children: the reward, the fruit of the womb.

segments.t: Cum déderit diléctis suis somnum: * ecce heréditas Dómini fílii: merces, fructus ventris.

content.latin: 126:4 Sicut sagíttæ in manu poténtis: * ita fílii excussórum.
content.english: 126:4 As arrows in the hand of the mighty, * so the children of them that have been shaken.

segments.t: Sicut sagíttæ in manu poténtis: * ita fílii excussórum.

content.latin: 126:5 Beátus vir, qui implévit desidérium suum ex ipsis: * non confundétur cum loquétur inimícis suis in porta.
content.english: 126:5 Blessed is the man that hath filled the desire with them; * he shall not be confounded when he shall speak to his enemies in the gate.

segments.t: Beátus vir, qui implévit desidérium suum ex ipsis: * non confundétur cum loquétur inimícis suis in porta.

content.latin: Pater noster, qui es in cælis, sanctificétur nomen tuum: advéniat regnum tuum: fiat volúntas tua, sicut in cælo et in terra. Panem nostrum cotidiánum da nobis hódie: et dimítte nobis débita nostra, sicut et nos dimíttimus debitóribus nostris: et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem: sed líbera nos a malo. Amen.

And forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us. And lead us not into temptation: But deliver us from evil. Amen.

Ídeo precor beátam Maríam semper Vírginem, beátum Michaélem Archángelum, beátum Ioánnem Baptístam, sanctos Apóstolos Petrum et Paulum, et omnes Sanctos, oráre pro me ad Dóminum Deum nostrum.
content.english: I confess to almighty God, to blessed Mary ever Virgin, to blessed Michael the Archangel, to blessed John the Baptist, to the holy Apostles Peter and Paul, and to all the Saints, that I have sinned exceedingly in thought, word and deed: strikes his breast through my fault, through my fault, through my most grievous fault. Therefore I beseech blessed Mary ever Virgin, blessed Michael the Archangel, blessed John the Baptist, the holy Apostles Peter and Paul, and all the Saints, to pray for me to the Lord our God.

content.english: 4:5 Be ye angry, and sin not: * the things you say in your hearts, be sorry for them upon your beds.

segments.t: Irascímini, et nolíte peccáre: * quæ dícitis in córdibus vestris, in cubílibus vestris compungímini.

content.latin: 4:6 Sacrificáte sacrifícium iustítiæ, et speráte in Dómino. * Multi dicunt: Quis osténdit nobis bona?
content.english: 4:6 Offer up the sacrifice of justice, and trust in the Lord: * many say, Who sheweth us good things?

segments.t: Sacrificáte sacrifícium iustítiæ, et speráte in Dómino. * Multi dicunt: Quis osténdit nobis bona?

content.latin: 4:7 Signátum est super nos lumen vultus tui, Dómine: * dedísti lætítiam in corde meo.
content.english: 4:7 The light of thy countenance, O Lord, is signed upon us: * thou hast given gladness in my heart.

segments.t: Signátum est super nos lumen vultus tui, Dómine: * dedísti lætítiam in corde meo.

content.latin: 4:8 A fructu fruménti, vini, et ólei sui * multiplicáti sunt.
content.english: 4:8 By the fruit of their corn, their wine, and oil, * they are multiplied.

segments.t: A fructu fruménti, vini, et ólei sui * multiplicáti sunt.

content.latin: 4:9 In pace in idípsum * dórmiam, et requiéscam;
content.english: 4:9 In peace in the selfsame * I will sleep, and I will rest:

segments.t: In pace in idípsum * dórmiam, et requiéscam;

content.latin: 4:10 Quóniam tu, Dómine, singuláriter in spe * constituísti me.
content.english: 4:10 For thou, O Lord, singularly * hast settled me in hope.

segments.t: Quóniam tu, Dómine, singuláriter in spe * constituísti me.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

segments.t: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

segments.t: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.

content.latin: Psalmus 90 [2]
content.english: Psalm 90 [2]

segments.t: Psalmus 90

content.latin: 90:1 Qui hábitat in adiutório Altíssimi, * in protectióne Dei cæli commorábitur.
content.english: 90:1 He that dwelleth in the aid of the most High, * shall abide under the protection of the God of Jacob.

segments.t: Qui hábitat in adiutório Altíssimi, * in protectióne Dei cæli commorábitur.

content.latin: 90:2 Dicet Dómino: Suscéptor meus es tu, et refúgium meum: * Deus meus sperábo in eum.
content.english: 90:2 He shall say to the Lord: Thou art my protector, and my refuge: * my God, in him will I trust.

segments.t: Dicet Dómino: Suscéptor meus es tu, et refúgium meum: * Deus meus sperábo in eum.

content.latin: 90:3 Quóniam ipse liberávit me de láqueo venántium, * et a verbo áspero.
content.english: 90:3 For he hath delivered me from the snare of the hunters: * and from the sharp word.

segments.t: Quóniam ipse liberávit me de láqueo venántium, * et a verbo áspero.

content.latin: 90:4 Scápulis suis obumbrábit tibi: * et sub pennis eius sperábis.
content.english: 90:4 He will overshadow thee with his shoulders: * and under his wings thou shalt trust.

segments.t: Scápulis suis obumbrábit tibi: * et sub pennis eius sperábis.

content.latin: 90:5 Scuto circúmdabit te véritas eius: * non timébis a timóre noctúrno,
content.english: 90:5 His truth shall compass thee with a shield: * thou shalt not be afraid of the terror of the night.

segments.t: Scuto circúmdabit te véritas eius: * non timébis a timóre noctúrno,

content.latin: 90:6 A sagítta volánte in die, a negótio perambulánte in ténebris: * ab incúrsu, et dæmónio meridiáno.
content.english: 90:6 Of the arrow that flieth in the day, of the business that walketh about in the dark: * of invasion, or of the noonday devil.

segments.t: A sagítta volánte in die, a negótio perambulánte in ténebris: * ab incúrsu, et dæmónio meridiáno.

content.latin: 90:7 Cadent a látere tuo mille, et decem míllia a dextris tuis: * ad te autem non appropinquábit.
content.english: 90:7 A thousand shall fall at thy side, and ten thousand at thy right hand: * but it shall not come nigh thee.

segments.t: Cadent a látere tuo mille, et decem míllia a dextris tuis: * ad te autem non appropinquábit.

content.latin: 90:8 Verúmtamen óculis tuis considerábis: * et retributiónem peccatórum vidébis.
content.english: 90:8 But thou shalt consider with thy eyes: * and shalt see the reward of the wicked.

segments.t: Verúmtamen óculis tuis considerábis: * et retributiónem peccatórum vidébis.

content.latin: 90:9 Quóniam tu es, Dómine, spes mea: * Altíssimum posuísti refúgium tuum.
content.english: 90:9 Because thou, O Lord, art my hope: * thou hast made the most High thy refuge.

segments.t: Quóniam tu es, Dómine, spes mea: * Altíssimum posuísti refúgium tuum.

content.latin: 90:10 Non accédet ad te malum: * et flagéllum non appropinquábit tabernáculo tuo.
content.english: 90:10 There shall no evil come to thee: * nor shall the scourge come near thy dwelling.

segments.t: Non accédet ad te malum: * et flagéllum non appropinquábit tabernáculo tuo.

content.latin: 90:11 Quóniam Ángelis suis mandávit de te: * ut custódiant te in ómnibus viis tuis.
content.english: 90:11 For he hath given his angels charge over thee; * to keep thee in all thy ways.

segments.t: Quóniam Ángelis suis mandávit de te: * ut custódiant te in ómnibus viis tuis.

content.latin: 90:12 In mánibus portábunt te: * ne forte offéndas ad lápidem pedem tuum.
content.english: 90:12 In their hands they shall bear thee up: * lest thou dash thy foot against a stone.

segments.t: In mánibus portábunt te: * ne forte offéndas ad lápidem pedem tuum.

content.latin: 90:13 Super áspidem, et basilíscum ambulábis: * et conculcábis leónem et dracónem.
content.english: 90:13 Thou shalt walk upon the asp and the basilisk: * and thou shalt trample under foot the lion and the dragon.

segments.t: Super áspidem, et basilíscum ambulábis: * et conculcábis leónem et dracónem.

content.latin: 90:14 Quóniam in me sperávit, liberábo eum: * prótegam eum, quóniam cognóvit nomen meum.
content.english: 90:14 Because he hoped in me I will deliver him: * I will protect him because he hath known my name.

segments.t: Quóniam in me sperávit, liberábo eum: * prótegam eum, quóniam cognóvit nomen meum.

content.latin: 90:15 Clamábit ad me, et ego exáudiam eum: * cum ipso sum in tribulatióne: erípiam eum et glorificábo eum.
content.english: 90:15 He shall cry to me, and I will hear him: * I am with him in tribulation, I will deliver him, and I will glorify him.

segments.t: Clamábit ad me, et ego exáudiam eum: * cum ipso sum in tribulatióne: erípiam eum et glorificábo eum.

content.latin: 90:16 Longitúdine diérum replébo eum: * et osténdam illi salutáre meum.
content.english: 90:16 I will fill him with length of days; * and I will shew him my salvation.

segments.t: Longitúdine diérum replébo eum: * et osténdam illi salutáre meum.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

segments.t: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

segments.t: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.

content.latin: Psalmus 133 [3]
content.english: Psalm 133 [3]

segments.t: Psalmus 133

content.latin: 133:1 Ecce nunc benedícite Dóminum, * omnes servi Dómini:
content.english: 133:1 Behold now bless ye the Lord, * all ye servants of the Lord:

segments.t: Ecce nunc benedícite Dóminum, * omnes servi Dómini:

content.latin: 133:1 Qui statis in domo Dómini, * in átriis domus Dei nostri.
content.english: 133:1 Who stand in the house of the Lord, * in the courts of the house of our God.

segments.t: Qui statis in domo Dómini, * in átriis domus Dei nostri.

content.latin: 133:2 In nóctibus extóllite manus vestras in sancta, * et benedícite Dóminum.
content.english: 133:2 In the nights lift up your hands to the holy places, * and bless ye the Lord.

segments.t: In nóctibus extóllite manus vestras in sancta, * et benedícite Dóminum.

content.latin: 133:3 Benedícat te Dóminus ex Sion, * qui fecit cælum et terram.
content.english: 133:3 May the Lord out of Sion bless thee, * he that made heaven and earth.

segments.t: Benedícat te Dóminus ex Sion, * qui fecit cælum et terram.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

segments.t: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

segments.t: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.

content.latin: Ant. Miserére mihi, Dómine, et exáudi oratiónem meam.
content.english: Ant. Have mercy on me, O Lord, and hear my prayer.

segments.t: Ant.
Miserére mihi, Dómine, et exáudi oratiónem meam.

content.latin: Te lucis ante términum,
content.english: Before the ending of the day,

content.latin: Rerum Creátor, póscimus,
content.english: Creator of the world, we pray

content.latin: Ut pro tua cleméntia
content.english: That with thy wonted favor thou

content.latin: Sis præsul et custódia.
content.english: Wouldst be our guard and keeper now.

content.latin: Procul recédant sómnia,
content.english: From all ill dreams defend our eyes,

content.latin: Et nóctium phantásmata;
content.english: From nightly fears and fantasies;

content.latin: Hostémque nostrum cómprime,
content.english: Tread under foot our ghostly foe,

content.latin: Ne polluántur córpora.
content.english: That no pollution we may know.

content.latin: Præsta, Pater piíssime,
content.english: O Father, that we ask be done,

content.latin: Patríque compar Únice,
content.english: Through Jesus Christ, thine only Son;

content.latin: Cum Spíritu Paráclito
content.english: Who, with the Holy Ghost and thee,

content.latin: Regnans per omne sǽculum.
content.english: Doth live and reign eternally.

content.latin: Amen.
content.english: Amen.

content.latin: Ier 14:9
content.english: Jer 14:9

segments.t: Ier 14:9

content.latin: Tu autem in nobis es, Dómine, et nomen sanctum tuum invocátum est super nos: ne derelínquas nos, Dómine, Deus noster.
content.english: But thou, O Lord, art among us, and thy name is called upon by us: forsake us not, O Lord our God.

content.latin: ℟. Deo grátias.
content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

segments.t: Deo grátias.

content.latin: ℟.br. In manus tuas, Dómine, * Comméndo spíritum meum.
content.english: ℟.br. Into thy hands, O Lord, * do I commend my spirit.

segments.t: ℟.br.
In manus tuas, Dómine, * Comméndo spíritum meum.

content.latin: ℟. In manus tuas, Dómine, * Comméndo spíritum meum.
content.english: ℟. Into thy hands, O Lord, * do I commend my spirit.

segments.t: In manus tuas, Dómine, * Comméndo spíritum meum.

content.latin: ℣. Redemísti nos, Dómine, Deus veritátis.
content.english: ℣. For thou hast redeemed us, O Lord, God of truth.

segments.t: Redemísti nos, Dómine, Deus veritátis.

content.latin: ℟. Comméndo spíritum meum.
content.english: ℟. I commend my spirit.

segments.t: Comméndo spíritum meum.

content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

segments.t: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

content.latin: ℟. In manus tuas, Dómine, * Comméndo spíritum meum.
content.english: ℟. Into thy hands, O Lord, * do I commend my spirit.

segments.t: In manus tuas, Dómine, * Comméndo spíritum meum.

content.latin: ℣. Custódi nos, Dómine, ut pupíllam óculi.
content.english: ℣. Keep us, Lord, as the apple of thine eye.

segments.t: Custódi nos, Dómine, ut pupíllam óculi.

content.latin: ℟. Sub umbra alárum tuárum prótege nos.
content.english: ℟. Protect us under the shadow of thy wings.

segments.t: Sub umbra alárum tuárum prótege nos.

content.latin: Ant. Salva nos, * Dómine, vigilántes, custódi nos dormiéntes; ut vigilémus cum Christo, et requiescámus in pace.
content.english: Ant. Protect us, * Lord, while we are awake and safeguard us while we sleep; that we may keep watch with Christ, and rest in peace.

segments.t: Ant.
Salva nos, * Dómine, vigilántes, custódi nos dormiéntes; ut vigilémus cum Christo, et requiescámus in pace.

content.latin: Canticum Simeonis
content.english: Canticle of Simeon

segments.t: Canticum Simeonis

content.latin: 2:29 Nunc dimíttis ✠ servum tuum, Dómine, * secúndum verbum tuum in pace:
content.english: 2:29 Now thou dost dismiss thy servant, O Lord, ✠ * according to thy word in peace;

segments.t: Nunc dimíttis ✠ servum tuum, Dómine, * secúndum verbum tuum in pace:

content.latin: 2:30 Quia vidérunt óculi mei * salutáre tuum,
content.english: 2:30 Because my eyes have seen * thy salvation,

segments.t: Quia vidérunt óculi mei * salutáre tuum,

content.latin: 2:31 Quod parásti * ante fáciem ómnium populórum,
content.english: 2:31 Which thou hast prepared * before the face of all peoples:

segments.t: Quod parásti * ante fáciem ómnium populórum,

content.latin: 2:32 Lumen ad revelatiónem géntium, * et glóriam plebis tuæ Israël.
content.english: 2:32 A light to the revelation of the Gentiles, * and the glory of thy people Israel.

segments.t: Lumen ad revelatiónem géntium, * et glóriam plebis tuæ Israël.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

segments.t: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

segments.t: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.

content.latin: Ant. Salva nos, Dómine, vigilántes, custódi nos dormiéntes; ut vigilémus cum Christo, et requiescámus in pace.
content.english: Ant. Protect us, Lord, while we are awake and safeguard us while we sleep; that we may keep watch with Christ, and rest in peace.

segments.t: Ant.
Salva nos, Dómine, vigilántes, custódi nos dormiéntes; ut vigilémus cum Christo, et requiescámus in pace.

content.latin: ℣. Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam.
content.english: ℣. O Lord, hear my prayer.

segments.t: Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam.

content.latin: ℟. Et clamor meus ad te véniat.
content.english: ℟. And let my cry come unto thee.

segments.t: Et clamor meus ad te véniat.

content.latin: Orémus.
content.english: Let us pray.

content.latin: Vísita, quǽsumus, Dómine, habitatiónem istam, et omnes insídias inimíci ab ea longe repélle: Ángeli tui sancti hábitent in ea, qui nos in pace custódiant; et benedíctio tua sit super nos semper.
content.english: Visit, we beseech thee, O Lord, this dwelling, and drive far from it the snares of the enemy; let thy holy angels dwell herein to preserve us in peace, and let thy blessing be always upon us.

content.latin: Per Dóminum nostrum Iesum Christum, Fílium tuum: qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
content.english: Through Jesus Christ, thy Son our Lord, Who liveth and reigneth with thee, in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

segments.t: Amen.

content.latin: ℣. Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam.
content.english: ℣. O Lord, hear my prayer.

segments.t: Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam.

content.latin: ℟. Et clamor meus ad te véniat.
content.english: ℟. And let my cry come unto thee.

segments.t: Et clamor meus ad te véniat.

content.latin: ℣. Benedicámus Dómino.
content.english: ℣. Let us bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedicámus Dómino.

content.latin: ℟. Deo grátias.
content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

segments.t: Deo grátias.

content.latin: Benedictio. Benedícat et custódiat nos omnípotens et miséricors Dóminus, ✠ Pater, et Fílius, et Spíritus Sanctus.
content.english: Benediction. The almighty and merciful Lord, ✠ the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit, bless us and keep us.

segments.t: Benedictio.
Benedícat et custódiat nos omnípotens et miséricors Dóminus, ✠ Pater, et Fílius, et Spíritus Sanctus.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

segments.t: Amen.

content.latin: Alma Redemptóris Mater, quæ pérvia cæli
content.english: Mother of Christ, hear thou thy people's cry

content.latin: Porta manes, et stella maris, succúrre cadénti,
content.english: Star of the deep and Portal of the sky!

content.latin: Súrgere qui curat, pópulo: tu quæ genuísti,
content.english: Mother of Him who thee from nothing made.

content.latin: Natúra miránte, tuum sanctum Genitórem,
content.english: Sinking we strive and call to thee for aid:

content.latin: Virgo prius ac postérius, Gabriélis ab ore
content.english: O, by what joy which Gabriel brought to thee,

content.latin: Sumens illud Ave, peccatórum miserére.
content.english: Thou Virgin first and last, let us thy mercy see.

content.latin: ℣. Post partum, Virgo, invioláta permansísti.
content.english: ℣. After childbirth thou didst remain a virgin.

segments.t: Post partum, Virgo, invioláta permansísti.

content.latin: ℟. Dei Génetrix, intercéde pro nobis.
content.english: ℟. Intercede for us, O Mother of God.

segments.t: Dei Génetrix, intercéde pro nobis.

content.latin: Orémus.
content.english: Let us pray.

content.latin: Deus, qui salútis ætérnæ, beátæ Maríæ virginitáte fecúnda, humáno géneri prǽmia præstitísti: tríbue, quǽsumus; ut ipsam pro nobis intercédere sentiámus, per quam merúimus auctórem vitæ suscípere, Dóminum nostrum Iesum Christum Fílium tuum. Amen.
content.english: O God, who, by the fruitful virginity of blessed Mary, hast bestowed upon mankind the reward of eternal salvation: grant, we beseech thee, that we may experience her intercession, through whom we have been made worthy to receive the author of life, Our Lord Jesus Christ thy Son. Amen.

content.latin: ℣. Divínum auxílium ✠ máneat semper nobíscum.
content.english: ℣. May the divine assistance ✠ remain with us always.

segments.t: Divínum auxílium ✠ máneat semper nobíscum.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

segments.t: Amen.
